name: MedNeXt
what: Transformer-inspired modernized ConvNeXt encoder-decoder for medical segmentation with residual up/down-sampling blocks, iteratively growing kernel sizes to avoid performance saturation on limited data, and compound scaling of depth/width/kernel size (MICCAI 2023).
why_better: Old plan commits to a Swin-Transformer multi-task trunk, whose quadratic attention is hard to train on ~70 labels and slow on CPU; MedNeXt gives long-range context via large conv kernels instead of attention, so SOTA-competitive accuracy is kept with a conv-only net that exports cleanly to ONNX Runtime CPU - cause: conv-only inductive bias, effect: robustness at 70 labels plus trivial ONNX deployment.
evidence: State-of-the-art on 4 CT/MRI tasks at varying dataset sizes (abstract; per-task numbers unverified); third-party BraTS-2024 SSA submission with MedNeXt ensemble: DSC 0.896 (arXiv 2411.15872).
source_title: MedNeXt: Transformer-driven Scaling of ConvNets for Medical Image Segmentation
fit_small_data: high - explicitly designed for data-scarce medical settings; iterative kernel growth targets saturation on limited data.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - pure convolutions, no attention/SSM; large kernels raise FLOPs, so use a small compound-scaling variant for the CPU student.
risk: codebase is 3D-first (2D adaptation must be validated); large-kernel blocks increase CPU latency; multi-head (soma+neurite+skeleton) not provided by authors.

name: nnU-Net Revisited benchmark (ResEnc/ConvNeXt presets)
what: MICCAI 2024 re-benchmark of CNN, Transformer, and Mamba segmentation methods that controls for inadequate baselines, insufficient datasets, and neglected compute; finds CNN U-Net variants (ResNet, ConvNeXt/ResEnc) in the nnU-Net framework, scaled to modern hardware, achieve SOTA and that most newer-architecture superiority claims do not survive scrutiny.
why_better: The old plan's Swin-Transformer choice rests on superiority claims that this benchmark shows often fail under proper controls; swapping the Swin head for the ResEnc/ConvNeXt U-Net presets (resenc/convnext variants in nnU-Net v2) lowers architecture risk for 70 labels and keeps ONNX CPU inference fast - cause: validated CNN+framework recipe, effect: same-or-better Dice with less risk and faster CPU inference.
evidence: Conclusion: CNN-based U-Nets (ResNet, ConvNeXt) + nnU-Net framework + compute scaling beat Transformer/Mamba claims across their benchmark (abstract; per-dataset numbers unverified).
source_title: nnU-Net Revisited: A Call for Rigorous Validation in 3D Medical Image Segmentation
code_url: none (results integrated in the nnU-Net repo; unverified)
fit_small_data: high - data-driven configuration and CNN inductive bias are proven on small medical datasets; the paper's lesson is that compute scaling beats novelty for a given dataset.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - ResEnc/ConvNeXt are conv-only and export to ONNX cleanly.
risk: benchmark is 3D CT/MRI, not 2D microscopy; the protocol must be re-run on our own data (proper folds, matched compute) before it is treated as a verdict for our task.

name: Primus / PrimusV2
what: First competitive Transformer-centric 3D segmentation models inside nnU-Net (TMLR 2025); high-resolution tokens with new positional-embedding and block design; PrimusV2 adds iterative patch embedding; Primus competes with default nnU-Net, PrimusV2 matches ResEnc-L and MedNeXt.
why_better: If the group still wants a transformer beyond Swin, PrimusV2 is the one validated in the same benchmarking culture as nnU-Net and it is shipped as an nnU-Net preset, so the Swin-Transformer trunk can be replaced with a drop-in preset whose superiority over default nnU-Net is demonstrated, instead of an unvalidated hand-built Swin multi-task model.
evidence: PrimusV2 exceeds default nnU-Net and is on par with ResEnc-L and MedNeXt across nine public datasets (abstract; per-dataset numbers unverified).
source_title: Primus: Enforcing Attention Usage for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
fit_small_data: medium - the paper itself documents transformers underperforming with limited data; on ~70 labels PrimusV2 likely ties or loses to ResEnc/ConvNeXt; 3D-to-2D transfer unverified.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - attention at high-resolution tokens exports to ONNX but is slower on CPU than a conv-only model of similar size.
risk: 3D codebase; ONNX attention overhead; no microscopy evaluation found in search; multi-head adaptation still DIY.

name: U-Mamba
what: U-shaped hybrid CNN-SSM network (MICCAI 2024) combining local conv features with Mamba's linear-complexity long-range modeling, with a self-configuring mechanism; evaluated on CT/MRI organ segmentation, endoscopy, and cell segmentation in microscopy images.
why_better: Replaces Swin's quadratic-attention trunk with linear-complexity SSM modeling of long-range dependencies (important for connected, branching neurites) at lower inference cost, and it is one of the few SSM papers with an actual microscopy cell-segmentation evaluation - cause: linear-complexity long-range context, effect: cheaper global modeling than Swin for thin elongated structures.
evidence: Outperforms state-of-the-art CNN and Transformer segmentation networks across four tasks including cell segmentation in microscopy (abstract; numbers unverified).
source_title: U-Mamba: Enhancing Long-range Dependency for Biomedical Image Segmentation
fit_small_data: medium - long-range SSM context plausibly helps thin connected neurites, but nnU-Net Revisited shows Mamba superiority claims often fail under matched compute; 70 labels is a small sample either way.
fit_onnx_cpu: low - selective scan relies on custom CUDA kernels; no ONNX/ONNX-Runtime support surfaced in any search; expect a slow or non-portable CPU deployment unless the scan is re-implemented as ops.
risk: ONNX export / CPU deployment is the blocker; research-grade code; soma-instance + neurite + skeleton multi-head must be built from scratch.

name: Mamba-UNet
what: UNet-like pure Visual Mamba (VMamba) encoder-decoder with skip connections and an integration mechanism between encoder/decoder paths (ACDC cardiac MRI, Synapse CT abdomen).
why_better: The pure-SSM variant (no conv trunk) isolates whether Mamba alone can replace the CNN backbone; if it ties the CNN at lower FLOPs it becomes a candidate large teacher to distill into a conv ONNX student - but it only matters if U-Mamba's export problem is solved, hence watch rather than trial.
evidence: Outperforms several UNet variants under identical hyperparameters on ACDC and Synapse (abstract; numbers unverified).
source_title: Mamba-UNet: UNet-Like Pure Visual Mamba for Medical Image Segmentation
code_url: none (stated available; URL not given in abstract, unverified)
fit_small_data: medium - same Mamba caveats as U-Mamba; no microscopy evaluation in the abstract.
fit_onnx_cpu: low - pure SSM: same selective-scan ONNX/CPU portability problem as U-Mamba.
risk: deployment path to ONNX Runtime CPU unproven; effort overlaps U-Mamba with weaker evidence - do not pursue both.

name: STU-Net
what: Scalable nnU-Net variants from 14M to 1.4B parameters trained on the large-scale TotalSegmentator dataset, evaluated on 14 downstream datasets for direct inference and 3 for fine-tuning across modalities.
why_better: Gives a ready-made, large, pre-trained teacher inside the same nnU-Net framework for the distillation step: instead of training a Swin teacher from scratch on 70 labels, fine-tune a pre-trained STU-Net variant and distill a small conv ONNX student - cause: large-scale supervised pre-training, effect: stronger features under a tiny label budget.
evidence: 14M-1.4B parameter series; good transfer in direct inference (14 datasets) and fine-tuning (3 datasets) (abstract; numbers unverified).
source_title: STU-Net: Scalable and Transferable Medical Image Segmentation Models Empowered by Large-Scale Supervised Pre-training
fit_small_data: medium - pre-training helps small-data fine-tuning, but TotalSegmentator is CT/MRI anatomy, far from 2D phase-contrast neurons; expect only partial feature transfer.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - conv nnU-Net family is ONNX-friendly, but the 1.4B teacher is GPU-only (fits A5000 with care); small pre-trained variants (14-78M) can serve as CPU deployable models.
risk: domain gap (anatomical CT/MRI to brightfield neurons); 3D codebase, 2D port DIY; 1.4B teacher training on 24GB may need patch/precision compromises.

name: CellViT / CellViT++
what: Vision-Transformer-based nuclei instance segmentation that leverages large-scale in-domain and out-of-domain pretrained ViT encoders (SAM plus a ViT pre-trained on 104M histological patches); CellViT++ is the improved model combined with nnU-Net in the PUMA melanoma challenge within a 24-hour development window.
why_better: Targets the soma instance objective (soma IoU >= 0.85) with a ViT instance head and pretrained encoder instead of a from-scratch Swin multi-task trunk - cause: in-domain pretrained encoder + dedicated instance head, effect: higher instance quality at low integration cost (proven 24h pipeline with nnU-Net).
evidence: PanNuke: mean panoptic quality 0.50, F1-detection 0.83 (arXiv 2306.15350); PUMA challenge: tissue Dice 0.750 vs baseline 0.629, nuclei comparable to baseline (arXiv 2503.12269).
source_title: Cracking the PUMA Challenge in 24 Hours with CellViT++ and nnU-Net
fit_small_data: medium - pretrained ViT encoder helps under few labels, but pre-training is on H&E histology, a different modality than phase-contrast neurons; transfer unverified for us.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - ViT attention is ONNX-exportable but heavier at equal resolution than conv-only; the CellViT++ + nnU-Net split keeps the instance head small.
risk: H&E-to-phase-contrast domain gap; instance head must handle brightfield somas with overlapping neurites and low contrast; not a neurite model (pair with a separate neurite branch).

name: DINOv3 (frozen dense encoder)
what: Meta's 2025 self-supervised vision foundation model (ViT suite) with Gram anchoring that fixes degradation of dense feature maps during long training, plus post-hoc strategies for resolution/size flexibility; claims to outperform specialized state of the art across many settings without fine-tuning.
why_better: Direct upgrade of the DINOv2 mentioned in the old plan: stronger, resolution-flexible dense features from one frozen ViT can drive both a soma and a neurite segmentation head (and the pre-annotator), reducing dependence on a task-specific Swin trunk trained from scratch - cause: better dense SSL features, effect: higher ceiling per labelled pixel at 70 images.
evidence: Outperforms specialized state of the art across a broad range of settings without fine-tuning (abstract; per-task numbers unverified).
fit_small_data: high - SSL foundation features are few-shot by construction; no pre-training on our data required.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - small ViT variants (ViT-S) are acceptable on CPU; larger variants are heavy; freeze encoder + small head to keep the ONNX graph small.
risk: pre-trained on natural images - no microscopy guarantee in the paper (adaptability shown indirectly by DINOCell/NeurINO); ViT attention latency on CPU; license of weights must be checked before shipping in a desktop app.

name: DINOCell
category: SSL pre-training strategy for cell segmentation
what: Self-supervised framework that continues DINOv2 training on unlabeled cell images (domain-adaptive pre-training) before supervised fine-tuning for cell instance segmentation, addressing the misalignment between natural-image SAM priors and microscopy.
why_better: Exploits the unlabelled image pool the old plan only uses for pseudo-labels: SSL-continued pre-training on our own unlabeled phase-contrast cells, then fine-tuning on ~70 labels, beats SAM-initialized models by +10.42% SEG on LIVECell - cause: domain-matched dense features before the supervised stage, effect: materially better small-data segmentation than zero-shot/fine-tuned foundation model baselines.
evidence: LIVECell SEG score 0.784, a 10.42% improvement over leading SAM-based models; strong zero-shot on three out-of-distribution microscopy datasets (abstract).
source_title: Self-supervised Pretraining of Cell Segmentation Models
fit_small_data: high - built for scarce labelled data; uses the unlabelled pool directly; largest measured small-data gain found in this search for cell segmentation.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - DINOv2 ViT backbone is ONNX-exportable; freeze it and add a light segmentation head for CPU deployment.
risk: SSL continued pre-training needs GPU time and schedule; code availability unverified; LIVECell is fluorescence, phase-contrast transfer unverified.

name: NeurINO (NeuroSeg Meets DINOv3)
what: CVPR 2026 framework that transfers 2D DINOv3 self-supervised priors into 3D neuron segmentation by inflating 2D filters into 3D operators, and introduces a topology-aware skeleton loss enforcing structural fidelity of graph-based neuronal arborization.
why_better: The old plan treats skeleton as a separate multi-task output supervised by clDice; NeurINO shows explicit topology-aware skeleton supervision on a foundation-model-initialized network yields ~3% absolute structure-accuracy gains on neuron data - cause: skeleton-graph topology enforced in the loss, effect: better neurite connectivity/branching (directly feeding length, branch count, and branch-angle metrics) with a data-efficient DINOv3-init recipe we can reuse in 2D.
evidence: Four neuronal datasets (2 BigNeuron, NeuroFly, CWMBS): average +2.9% Entire Structure Average, +2.8% Different Structure Average, +3.8% Percentage of Different Structure over SoTA (abstract).
source_title: NeuroSeg Meets DINOv3: Transferring 2D Self-Supervised Visual Priors to 3D Neuron Segmentation via DINOv3 Initialization
fit_small_data: medium - data-efficiency claim comes with foundation-model initialization; transfer to 2D brightfield PC12 images is unverified.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - the full model is a 3D DINOv3-based net (heavy); the portable asset is the topology-aware skeleton loss plus the DINOv3-init idea, both cheap in a 2D conv student.
risk: 3D codebase; gains measured on fluorescence 3D neurons, not 2D phase contrast; integrating the graph-based loss into our multi-task training is non-trivial.

name: Skea-Topo Aware loss
what: IJCAI 2024 skeleton-based loss for reticular boundary segmentation: a skeleton-aware weighted term that models object geometry via skeletons, plus a boundary-rectification term that emphasizes topologically critical pixels using both ground-truth and predicted skeletons.
why_better: Upgrades the old plan's clDice-only topology term: weighting supervision along skeleton pixels directly targets connectivity and branch-point fidelity of 2-3 px neurites, where Dice is insensitive to topology errors - cause: pixel weights proportional to topological significance, effect: fewer broken/merged neurites (protecting length and branch-count accuracy) with a loss-only change, no architecture risk, ONNX-identical inference.
evidence: Improves topological consistency by up to 7 VI points compared with 13 state-of-the-art methods across three boundary segmentation datasets (abstract).
source_title: Enhancing Boundary Segmentation for Topological Accuracy with Skeleton-based Methods
fit_small_data: high - loss only; adds no parameters or data requirements.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - training-time only; skeleton computation can be precomputed offline and inference graph is unchanged.
risk: needs skeleton labels during training (our plan already produces them for NETMORPH); gains were measured on reticular boundaries (membrane/grain/road), neurite-specific transfer unverified.

name: KDAS (attention-supervised knowledge distillation)
category: knowledge distillation (large teacher to compact ONNX student)
what: Knowledge-distillation framework for (polyp) segmentation that adds attention supervision and a Symmetrical Guiding Module to align teacher and student features, producing compact student models with fewer parameters.
why_better: The old plan only mentions distillation vaguely ('small NN' for NTI); KDAS gives a concrete recipe to distill a larger multi-task teacher (MedNeXt / pre-trained STU-Net / DINOv3-init ViT) into a small conv ONNX student for offline CPU inference - cause: attention supervision mitigates teacher-student feature mismatch, effect: a student that approaches teacher quality with a CPU-deployable footprint, the exact large-to-small gap this project must close.
evidence: Compact students achieve competitive results with state-of-the-art polyp segmentation methods (abstract; numbers unverified).
source_title: KDAS: Knowledge Distillation via Attention Supervision Framework for Polyp Segmentation
fit_small_data: high - KD is a standard small-data lever; attention guidance helps most when labels are scarce.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - student is a compact conv (UNet-like) network; ONNX-friendly by construction.
risk: requires a genuinely better teacher first (which must be established at 70 labels); two-stage teacher-then-student schedule consumes part of the 15-week window.

name: OpenPhenom
what: CZI's cell-painting foundation model - a self-supervised ViT trained on ~2.2M fluorescence cell images producing phenotype embeddings - benchmarked against DINOv3 ViT-B/16 and SubCell across four evaluation protocols on JUMP-CP, RxRx1, and RxRx3-core (CP-BG-Bench).
why_better: Offers a microscopy-domain alternative to DINOv2/DINOv3 for the encoder stage, specifically for the fluorescence channel used in label checking, where a domain-pretrained encoder should need less fine-tuning than a natural-image ViT - cause: pre-training on 2.2M fluorescence cell images, effect: potentially fewer labelled examples needed for the fluorescence-verification head; worth a benchmark comparison against DINOv3 on our unlabelled pool.
evidence: CP-BG-Bench (2609.12761): four protocols rank OpenPhenom / DINOv3 / SubCell systematically differently on three datasets, so the right encoder is protocol-dependent (no single number transferable to us); OpenPhenom trained on 2.2M images per CWA-MSN (2509.19896).
source_title: Same Encoder, Different Winner: A Paired-View Framework for Cell Painting Encoder Evaluation
code_url: none (no arXiv paper for OpenPhenom itself; official repo github.com/CZI-scicomp/openphenom, unverified in this search)
fit_small_data: low - it is a representation model, not a segmentation model; domain match is fluorescence Cell Painting, not phase contrast.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - frozen ViT inference on CPU is fine for pre-annotation or feature extraction only, not full-frame segmentation at high resolution.
risk: would violate the no-learned-cell-embeddings-for-similarity constraint if used for NTI embeddings - only acceptable as a feature extractor for the fluorescence channel; phase-contrast vs fluorescence domain gap; license must be checked.

name: Cellpose-SAM CPU quantization (W8A16 / mixed W4/W8)
what: Deployment study (NeurIPS 2026 workshop) of compressed Cellpose-SAM for laboratory CPUs using a retention criterion: the 95% cluster-bootstrap interval of mean change from FP32 must stay above a fixed -0.02 margin per modality; W8A16 preserves instance F1, a sensitivity-guided mixed W4/W8 scheme with four INT8 exceptions achieves 6.76x weight reduction with 0/176 field failures, while ternary 12.08x fails on 169/176 fields.
why_better: The old plan uses Cellpose3 for pre-annotation with no CPU deployment strategy; this recipe quantifies how far a foundation-model pre-annotator can be compressed for the offline desktop constraint and shows the failure boundary (ternary is catastrophic) - cause: modality-stratified retention auditing instead of single-number accuracy, effect: a de-risked, auditable path to run the pre-annotator on CPU with 6.76x smaller weights.
evidence: Stratified 176-field panel (BBBC038 nuclei, BBBC039 U2OS fluorescence, NIST iPSC): W8A16 preserves instance F1 across all modalities; mixed W4/W8 = 6.76x weight reduction, 0/176 catastrophic failures; ternary 12.08x = 169/176 failures (abstract).
source_title: Retention-Constrained Post-Training Quantization of Cellpose-SAM for Stem Cell Microscopy
fit_small_data: high - orthogonal to label count; applies to the pre-annotation stage.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - explicitly targets CPU/edge deployment of a segmentation foundation model.
risk: single-author workshop paper; the retention protocol must be re-derived on our own phase-contrast panel before trusting W4/W8 numbers.
